title: Dreamland singers and how tips were shared
summary: George Dewey Washington and Walter Richardson sang at the Dreamland; tips were split among band and singers, unlike Alberta Hunter's reputed practice.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now when you were at the Dreamland, I meant to ask you, were there any singers with the band at the Dreamland?
Well, we had a fellow by the name of George Dewey Washington. Who was very popular and Walter Richardson.

George Dewey Washington, and Walter Richardson, would sing at the Dreamland, like he would have them come in on weekends and sing. And they were very, very famous singers in Chicago at that time. They also sang at the Vendome.
And when you performed as accompanying singers, the singers got the tips, didn't they?
No, those tips were all divided equally.
Among the band and the singers.

I see, cause Lil Armstrong used to tell me about when she was accompanying Alberta in those clubs, Alberta would go from table to table and pick up the tips and she was supposed, to of course, share them with the accompaniest, but Lil suspected that she didn't always get her share.
No, I imagine she didn't. Lot of them they would holdout, sure, cause there'd be a lot of money.

Well, the singers like that they thought they were working harder than the band, but actually the band was working just as hard because they stay out on the floor sometimes an hour or over an hour. Sure, there was an act called Brown and McGraw, jazz dancers.
